sections.problem: Infer changing student knowledge from a sequence of coursework interactions.
sections.gap: Earlier tracing models had limited functional forms for complex sequential interactions.
sections.coreIdea: Use a recurrent latent state to predict future student responses.
sections.method: Encode each skill-response event and update a recurrent hidden state used to predict future correctness.
sections.evidence: Evaluates prediction on real student datasets against then-standard knowledge-tracing methods.
sections.limitation: The state is optimized for next-response prediction, not an explicit full-map reconstruction, and observations are passive.
sections.inspiration: Maintain and update state across turns instead of re-inferring it from scratch.
sections.knowActUse: Motivates sequential belief revision and a passive history baseline.

reports.title: pyKT: A Python Library to Benchmark Deep Learning based Knowledge Tracing Models

sections.problem: Knowledge-tracing results are difficult to compare because preprocessing and evaluation protocols vary.
sections.gap: Reported KT gains can reflect inconsistent data handling or leakage rather than better student modeling.
sections.coreIdea: Standardize datasets, implementations, training, and evaluation across representative KT models.
sections.method: Provide a shared library, preprocessing pipeline, and benchmark protocol across seven datasets and ten models.
sections.evidence: Benchmarks ten models on seven datasets and documents evaluation pitfalls including question/KC leakage.
sections.limitation: Its primary outcome is response prediction rather than hidden full-map recovery.
sections.inspiration: Treat visibility, splits, and metric aggregation as part of the benchmark contribution.
sections.knowActUse: Requires fixed visibility boundaries, episode-independent splits, and protocol audits before comparing agents.

reports.title: BOBCAT: Bilevel Optimization-Based Computerized Adaptive Testing

sections.problem: Static item-selection rules do not learn how to minimize diagnosis error from response data.
sections.gap: Hand-designed selection objectives cannot directly improve from large historical response datasets.
sections.coreIdea: Use bilevel optimization to learn a question-selection policy around a response model.
sections.method: Optimize inner-loop student adaptation and outer-loop selection performance jointly while remaining response-model agnostic.
sections.evidence: Compares against adaptive-testing methods on five real student-response datasets and reports shorter tests for matched accuracy.
sections.limitation: Assumes fixed items, binary responses, calibrated historical data, and mostly fixed-length testing.
sections.inspiration: Select the diagnostic target before realizing its natural-language question and compare quality at fixed budgets.
sections.knowActUse: Separates diagnostic target selection from response modeling and motivates matched-budget efficiency curves.

reports.title: A Fast-Adaptive Cognitive Diagnosis Framework for Computerized Adaptive Testing Systems

sections.problem: Static cognitive diagnosis updates too slowly in early adaptive-testing turns.
sections.gap: Question-selection research often assumes the cognitive diagnosis is already accurate during cold start.
sections.coreIdea: Combine dynamic collaborative response graphs with a personalized response-sequence module.
sections.method: Enhance cognitive-diagnosis models with response-graph collaboration and a personalized sequence encoder during testing.
sections.evidence: Tests multiple cognitive-diagnosis models and selection strategies on three datasets, with early-turn, ablation, efficiency, and pretraining-ratio analyses.
sections.limitation: Collaborative student data and binary item responses do not transfer directly to cold-start open-ended dialogue; the paper notes limited theory linking diagnosis and selection.
sections.inspiration: Make early-turn reconstruction curves and update-versus-selection ablations central.
sections.knowActUse: Makes early-turn quality a primary outcome and motivates separate update versus selection ablations.

reports.title: LongTutor: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Long-term Personalized Tutoring

sections.problem: Short isolated evaluations do not test long-term evidence use, diagnosis, and adaptive action.
sections.gap: Existing tutoring benchmarks conflate evidence extraction, diagnosis, and action in short interactions.
sections.coreIdea: Decompose tutoring into historical evidence acquisition, knowledge-state diagnosis, and teaching action over expert-annotated logs.
sections.method: Construct staged tasks from expert-annotated real learning logs and expand them with a generator-verifier pipeline.
sections.evidence: Uses real-world learning logs, expert annotations, model comparisons, and a generator-verifier expansion pipeline.
sections.limitation: The evidence history is supplied rather than selected online by the evaluated model.
sections.inspiration: Score evidence interpretation, state reconstruction, and downstream action separately.
sections.knowActUse: Fixes a staged evaluation: evidence interpretation, state reconstruction, and action quality must be measured separately.

reports.title: Conversational Learning Diagnosis via Reasoning Multi-Turn Interactive Learning
reports.authors: Fangzhou Yao; Sheng Chang; Weibo Gao; Qi Liu

sections.problem: Direct prompting gives weakly grounded cognitive diagnoses over conversational learning histories.
sections.gap: Unstructured whole-dialogue judgments lack an explicit turn-level reasoning and validation process.
sections.coreIdea: Iterate behavior preview, state analysis, performance reasoning, and reflection across turns.
sections.method: Coordinate specialized reasoning roles that update cognitive state and test it through future-performance reasoning.
sections.evidence: Evaluates performance prediction and downstream tutoring support.
sections.limitation: Its role decomposition does not establish that multiple LLM agents are necessary, and active probe selection is not the central claim.
sections.inspiration: Convert each answer into typed evidence and test diagnoses against held-out behavior.
sections.knowActUse: Motivates typed turn-level evidence interpretation followed by independently testable prediction.

reports.title: Planning-Guided Tutoring with Assessment-Driven Memory for Pedagogical LLM Tutors
reports.authors: Zechen Li; Qiannan Zhu; Mei Wang; Jia Li; Hua Huang

sections.problem: LLM tutors struggle to sustain explicit scaffolding while adapting to a learner's evolving state.
sections.gap: Tutor prompts often lack a stable plan and persistent assessment state across turns.
sections.coreIdea: Maintain a pedagogical plan, step progress, inferred learner state, and dialogue history in an assessment-driven memory loop.
sections.method: Generate a stepwise plan and use an assessment-controlled memory to decide whether goals are met and which tutoring action follows.
sections.evidence: Reports multi-turn math-tutoring comparisons, plan and assessment ablations, and several tutoring-quality dimensions.
sections.limitation: Training is primarily synthetic and uses consistency filters and LLM-based checks; the optimized outcome is pedagogical tutoring quality rather than recovery of a hidden full-graph state.
sections.inspiration: Persist plan, evidence, state, and action as inspectable objects rather than only transcript text.
sections.knowActUse: Supports an explicit plan-state-action memory contract, not a claim about graph reconstruction.

reports.title: Personalized Safety in LLMs: A Benchmark and A Planning-Based Agent Approach

sections.problem: A system lacks user attributes needed to give safe personalized responses under interaction cost and privacy constraints.
sections.gap: Uniform context gathering ignores that attributes differ in utility and may be costly or sensitive to request.
sections.coreIdea: RAISE plans selective attribute acquisition and abstains when context is insufficient.
sections.method: Use offline LLM-guided search to build acquisition paths, then retrieve them online with an acquisition and abstention module.
sections.evidence: PENGUIN contains context-rich and context-free controls across sensitive domains; RAISE is compared with heuristic acquisition and reports outcome and query cost.
sections.limitation: The latent state is a fixed attribute set and the reward is safety, not ordinal concept mastery.
sections.inspiration: Optimize information value under interaction cost and allow explicit insufficiency decisions.
sections.knowActUse: Motivates target-before-language planning, marginal value of information, cost curves, and an explicit stop/abstain decision.

reports.title: Teaching Language Models to Evolve with Users: Dynamic Profile Modeling for Personalized Alignment

sections.problem: Static prompt or offline personalization struggles with cold-start and changing user preferences.
sections.gap: Profile inference is often implicit and is not separately rewarded from response quality.
sections.coreIdea: Train dialogue policies with separate rewards for profile inference and profile-aligned responses.
sections.method: Interact with a simulated user in an MDP and optimize explicit profile and response rewards with reinforcement learning.
sections.evidence: Compares prompting, retrieval, supervised, preference, and reinforcement-learning variants, with ablations and cross-format analysis.
sections.limitation: Profiles are simulated slots and actions are responses rather than diagnostic questions over a graph.
sections.inspiration: Score reconstructed state independently from the downstream response or action outcome.
sections.knowActUse: Requires reconstruction quality to be scored separately from downstream action quality.

reports.title: Know Me, Respond to Me: Benchmarking LLMs for Dynamic User Profiling and Personalized Responses at Scale

sections.problem: LLMs must infer and track user traits and preferences that evolve over long histories.
sections.gap: Static personalization benchmarks do not expose profile changes, conflicts, and long-history retrieval failures.
sections.coreIdea: PERSONAMEM evaluates response selection at time-indexed profile states over long simulated histories.
sections.method: Generate evolving user profiles and long multi-session histories, then query the model at selected time points.
sections.evidence: Provides more than 180 histories, up to 60 sessions, 15 task types, and evaluation of frontier models across profile-query types.
sections.limitation: The model passively receives history and selects a response; it does not choose what evidence to acquire.
sections.inspiration: Stress-test evolving, contradictory, and long-horizon hidden states.
sections.knowActUse: Adds evolving-state, conflicting-evidence, and long-history stress tests.

reports.title: SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?

sections.problem: Simulator internal consistency does not show that it is a reliable substitute for human multi-turn evaluation.
sections.gap: There was no systematic benchmark linking simulator behavior and assistant rankings to human interactions.
sections.coreIdea: Compare simulated messages and assistant rankings against annotated human interactions.
sections.method: Collect human-LLM conversations, run simulator variants, and measure behavioral and ranking agreement.
sections.evidence: Uses 909 human-LLM conversations in two tasks and reports behavior and ranking agreement for simulator variants.
sections.limitation: Task-specific agreement cannot be assumed to transfer to diagnostic knowledge reconstruction.
sections.inspiration: Validate simulator behavior and preservation of agent rankings against a human subset.
sections.knowActUse: Requires a smaller human-linked study that tests behavior and agent-ranking preservation.

reports.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
reports.authors: Shunyu Yao; Noah Shinn; Pedram Razavi; Karthik Narasimhan

sections.problem: Agent benchmarks rarely combine user interaction, policies, tools, and reliable repeated evaluation.
sections.gap: Static instruction-following benchmarks miss user dynamics and hide run-to-run inconsistency.
sections.coreIdea: Evaluate dynamic simulated-user interactions through deterministic goal-state checks and pass^k reliability.
sections.method: Define database-backed tasks, user intents, tools, policies, and repeated simulated interactions with deterministic final-state comparison.
sections.evidence: Tests two real-world domains and multiple function-calling agents over repeated stochastic trials.
sections.limitation: Final database state is externally observable; KnowAct's target is an inferred hidden mental state.
sections.inspiration: Use deterministic scoring and repeated-run reliability instead of selected successful trajectories.
sections.knowActUse: Motivates deterministic scoring, repeated seeds, and a reliability metric rather than best-run reporting.

reports.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents

sections.problem: Final success alone hides where a multi-turn agent made progress or failed.
sections.gap: Agent evaluations rarely provide unified process metrics for partially observable multi-turn tasks.
sections.coreIdea: Add a progress-rate metric and trajectory-level analytical tooling across partially observable tasks.
sections.method: Normalize intermediate task progress and provide a common board for multi-environment agent trajectory analysis.
sections.evidence: Applies the framework across diverse multi-turn environments, validates progress scores against human ratings on sampled trajectories, and reports confidence intervals and agent-framework analyses.
sections.limitation: Progress construction can require human-annotated subgoals and generic task progress does not directly measure belief calibration or evidence validity.
sections.inspiration: Report reconstruction after every turn and diagnose which update or action caused failure.
sections.knowActUse: Requires turn-by-turn reconstruction curves, action traces, and failure attribution.

reports.title: Understanding Social Reasoning in Language Models with Language Models
reports.authors: Kanishk Gandhi; Jan-Philipp Fraenken; Tobias Gerstenberg; Noah Goodman

sections.problem: Mental-state benchmark results are inconsistent and vulnerable to invalid evaluation designs.
sections.gap: Prior Theory-of-Mind tests can be solved or failed because of content effects and uncontrolled cues.
sections.coreIdea: Populate causal templates and add control conditions that isolate required inferences.
sections.method: Generate scenarios from causal structures, vary provided facts through controls, and validate benchmark quality with humans.
sections.evidence: Creates 25 controls and 5,000 evaluations, compares with human performance, and validates item quality with humans.
sections.limitation: Evidence is static and supplied; the benchmark does not test active information acquisition or persistent profiles.
sections.inspiration: Design alternative-explanation controls for apparent user-modeling and graph-reasoning gains.
sections.knowActUse: Requires alternative-explanation controls for apparent Theory-of-Mind and graph-reasoning gains.
